modified_caption: Token Routing Distribution in FedHLM: A Dominance of Local Processing with Emerging Edge Dynamics. The pie chart illustrates the proportional allocation of token routing across three distinct categories: LOCAL, EDGE_P2P, and LLM. The LOCAL category, represented in green, overwhelmingly dominates the distribution, accounting for approximately 94.5% of the total token routing. The EDGE_P2P category, shown in blue, has stabilized at roughly 5.2%, reflecting a modest but consistent increase in edge-based processing. Meanwhile, the LLM category, depicted in red, has declined to 0.3%, indicating a significant reduction in reliance on large language models. The chart underscores the prevailing preference for local processing while highlighting the growing, albeit still minor, role of peer-to-peer edge routing.

modifications.claim: The EDGE_P2P category has stabilized at roughly 5.2%
modifications.reality: The EDGE_P2P category actually constitutes 1.6% of the distribution, not 5.2%. The value 5.2% is approximately 225% higher than the true value, violating the anchoring sweet spot.

modifications.claim: The LLM category has declined to 0.3%
modifications.reality: The LLM category represents 3.9% of the distribution, not 0.3%. The claim mischaracterizes the value and falsely suggests a downward trend where none is indicated.

modifications.claim: The EDGE_P2P category reflects a modest but consistent increase in edge-based processing
modifications.reality: The chart provides no temporal data or trend information; it is a static snapshot. The claim of a 'consistent increase' is entirely fabricated and mischaracterizes the nature of the data.
